title: Constructive Lean 4 Formalization and Exact-Rational Certificates for Dynamic-Streaming Euclidean Diameter Bounds
abstract: Jeff Giliberti and MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi (arXiv:2611.33139, Nov. 24, 2026) resolved the update-time versus space tradeoff for high-dimensional Euclidean diameter in fully dynamic streams: for every fixed c > sqrt(3), their one-pass algorithm maintains a current witness pair with approximation factor c in O~(N^(1-eps_c) poly(d)) space (explicitly eps_2 = 10^-10 at c = 2) and worst-case update time poly(d, log N), while every constant-factor c-approximation requires N^Omega(1/(c^2 log(c+1))) words even on short binary set streams of at most 2N-1 updates. We present a standalone, zero-dependency Lean 4.35.0 formalization (EuclideanDiameterStreaming.lean) of 18 core algebraic, variance-hull, Cauchy-Schwarz, parallel-axis, nested-cap shrinkage, Appendix A.1 Table 3 factor-2 parameter, non-circular submodular diagonal-squared, and baseline positivity theorems (0 sorry, 0 warnings, 0 Classical.choice), paired with a zero-floating-point exact-Q four-mode certificate auditor (EUCLID-DIAM-CERT-1.0). Across 16 canonical certificates (0.129-3.412 ms), the auditor verifies an exact zero-slack 12-point two-simplex attainment in Q^13 (a = 13/7, diam(H_a(S))^2 = (289/49) diam(S)^2), Lemma 4.1 anchor-variance parallel-axis composition, all Appendix A.1 Table 3 factor-2 inequalities, and exhaustive Lemma 10.2 submodular diagonal-squared bounds D^2 <= 2sZ while rejecting 60/60 live adversarial forgeries.
